title: Japchae
subtitle: korean glass noodles with vegetables
excerpt: Japchae is a Korean stir-fried noodle dish made from sweet potato starch noodles, seasoned vegetables, and beef, all tossed in sesame oil and soy sauce. It is served warm or at room temperature. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Japchae was first made in the 17th century Korean royal court. Originally it was a vegetable dish without noodles. Glass noodles were added later and became the defining ingredient.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the noodles and vegetables up to 4 hours ahead. Toss together just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: Korean sweet potato starch noodles, also called glass noodles. They are translucent when cooked and have a firm, springy texture.
An oil pressed from toasted sesame seeds. It is rich and nutty and used as a seasoning in Korean and other East Asian cooking rather than as a cooking fat.

content.text: noodles that turn glossy and slightly chewy when cooked. They soak up the sesame and soy dressing well. Serves 4 as a side or 2 as a main.

items.prepNote: sweet potato starch glass noodles, soaked in cold water for 30 minutes

content.text: Drain the soaked noodles. Cook in a large pot of boiling water for 6 to 7 minutes until tender but still springy. Drain and rinse under cold water. Cut the noodles in half with scissors so they are easier to toss.
Combine the dressing ingredients in a large bowl. Add 2 tablespoons of the dressing to the warm noodles and toss to coat.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain, squeeze dry, and season with a little of the dressing. Set aside.

Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. If using beef, cook it quickly with a little garlic and 1 tsp soy sauce for 2 minutes. Remove and set aside. Cook the carrot for 2 minutes, then the onion for 3 minutes, then the mushrooms for 3 minutes, each in a separate turn with a little oil.
Add all the cooked vegetables, beef (if using), and spinach to the bowl of noodles. Pour over the remaining dressing. Toss everything together gently with tongs.
Scatter sesame seeds and spring onion over the top. Serve warm or at room temperature.

attrs.fix: Toss the noodles with 1 teaspoon of sesame oil immediately after draining. This prevents sticking before you add the dressing.
Japchae needs generous seasoning. Taste the final dish and add more soy sauce or sesame oil as needed. The noodles absorb a lot of flavour.
The noodles need a full soak before cooking. Soak in cold water for at least 30 minutes, then boil until fully tender.

content.text: Japchae is a celebration dish in Korea. It appears at birthdays, weddings, and holiday tables. It is also sold at street food stalls and packed into lunchboxes. The dish is served as a side or a main. It is one of the few Korean noodle dishes that is eaten at room temperature as well as warm.
